elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 3.4: "Customer may terminate for convenience this Agreement (including all Service Option Attachments) or any Service Option Attachment ..." The Agreement is defined to include the Order Forms and Service Option Attachments, so the Agreement-level and attachment-level convenience right covers the element; the retained prerequisite-attachment carve-out is pre-existing language, not a new restriction.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Sub-clause a. now reads "providing at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to IBM", and the original "at the end of any calendar month" effectiveness anchor was deleted so termination takes effect on the 30-day notice rather than being pushed to a month-end.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "IBM will refund prepaid charges for the period after the effective date of termination on a pro-rata basis." This is an express pro-rata basis (not merely a post-termination-period refund) and is tied to the Section 3.4 convenience exit.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: IBM's only exits in the cited text are material breach (3.3) and the Section 3.2 auto-renewal notice, which is expressly effective only "at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term" — natural-term non-renewal assessed under RENEWAL, not mid-term T4C. No mid-term Vendor convenience right appears, so the element is met as already-satisfied without any edit.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The rendered notice is "at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice", which is below the 60–90 day fallback band. (This is Customer-favourable and consistent with the preferred level being targeted.)

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: No cap is inserted anywhere in the operative text; the drafter concedes the Attachment A early termination charges remain uncapped ("We note but do not press a three-month cap"). A comment note is not operative language. The retained "; and" after sub-clause a. also signals an un-edited sub-clause b. (termination charges) that is left uncapped.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not bite: Vendor holds no convenience right at all. Its only unilateral exit is the Section 3.2 non-renewal notice whose effect is expressly tied to "the end of the then-current term", so nothing permits a mid-term Vendor convenience exit.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply because Vendor has no convenience right; in any event the only Vendor-side exit notice requires "at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term".

reasons: All four preferred elements are met in operative language: an express "Customer may terminate for convenience" right over the Agreement and any Service Option Attachment, a thirty (30) day notice with the month-end effectiveness anchor removed, an express pro-rata refund of prepaid charges for the post-termination period, and no Vendor mid-term convenience right (Section 3.2 is natural-term non-renewal, scored under RENEWAL).

The fallback level is incomplete (30-day notice sits outside the 60–90 day band and no three-month cap on early-termination charges is inserted), but position-completeness is satisfied at the preferred level, so this does not defeat the redline.

Minimality holds: three narrow operations (insert the convenience label, change one month to thirty (30) days, add the refund sentence). Deleting "at the end of any calendar month" is necessary to deliver the 30-day exit required by element 2, not a cosmetic cut. The prerequisite-attachment carve-out, the Section 3.4 continued-performance sentence, and Section 3.2 are all retained verbatim; no survival tail, expense language, or extra procedure was added.

Intent is preserved: Section 3.5's acceleration of accrued payment obligations is untouched and does not contradict a refund of unearned prepaid charges; no defined term, cross-reference, or commercial mechanic is left dangling by the edits.

Drafting caution (not a defect in the checked elements): the retained "; and" at the end of sub-clause a. indicates an un-rendered sub-clause b. If that sub-clause imposes Attachment A early termination charges, confirm it does not read as a penalty that offsets the new pro-rata refund; if it does, either cap it at three months' fees or state that the refund applies notwithstanding any termination charge.
